title: UniformConvergesOn: a one-constructor TYPE (not Prop) carrying the uniform rate as data
statement: CReal.UniformConvergesOn (F : Nat -> CReal -> CReal) (G : CReal -> CReal) (a b : CReal) is a one-constructor inductive family in Sort 1 (a Type, not a Prop): its single constructor packages a rate : Nat and a proof that for every eps, taking n >= rate puts F n within 1/(eps+1) of G uniformly on [a,b]. Deliberately Type-valued rather than Exists-wrapped Prop, because the theorem this definition exists to support (uniform_limit_uniformly_continuous) must CONSTRUCT a UniformlyContinuousOn value whose modulus field needs the convergence rate as literal Nat-building data, and Exists.rec is Prop-only -- it cannot eliminate a Prop-wrapped witness into a Type-valued construction. There is no pointwise-not-uniform counterexample checked in this kernel; the guarantee instead rests on a type-level argument: rate is a single Nat (not a function CReal -> Nat), so point-dependence of the convergence rate is syntactically impossible for any UniformConvergesOn witness, by construction of the type.
